capabilities.capability: allocator, assertion, clock, yield and hash hooks
capabilities.silex_contract: The compiler, STD and the host runtime own these process-wide facilities.
capabilities.rationale: They are Box2D C integration hooks, not rigid-body gameplay capabilities; exposing them would leak runtime plumbing into GFX.Physics.

capabilities.capability: engine version record
capabilities.silex_contract: Every differential corpus record names both engine versions and the immutable oracle revision.

capabilities.capability: generic trigonometry and rotation helpers
capabilities.silex_contract: Physics consumes STD.Math values instead of publishing an engine-specific math library.
capabilities.rationale: These functions support Box2D's C value model but are not physics-domain intentions.

capabilities.capability: world scale units
capabilities.silex_contract: GFX.Physics worlds use meters, seconds and kilograms without mutable process-global scaling.
capabilities.rationale: Boundary conversion preserves normalized physical observations at 1 and 100 application units per meter in the paired witness. Worlds retain meter-based tolerances; arbitrary-scale equivalence and mutable process-global units are not claimed.

capabilities.capability: finite and valid public geometry
capabilities.silex_contract: Constructors and public operations reject invalid values directly instead of requiring validation helper calls.
capabilities.rationale: Finite scalars/vectors, angle-derived rotations, ordered/degenerate AABBs and zero-motion/zero-fraction rays are qualified at public boundaries. Raw cosine/sine rotations are replaced by angles; planes are normalized collision results without a public general-plane constructor. The paired witnesses separate those representations and compare actual ray and shape-cast results; they do not claim a general boolean validation API.

capabilities.capability: default world configuration
capabilities.silex_contract: World2DSettings makes every developer-owned creation choice explicit with stable meter-second defaults.

capabilities.capability: default body configuration
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2DSettings owns stable typed defaults for creation-time body control.

capabilities.capability: default collider, chain, filter and material configuration
capabilities.silex_contract: Collider2DSettings, PhysicsMaterial2D, CollisionFilter2D and chain segment materials express these defaults as typed Silex values.

capabilities.capability: default spatial query filter
capabilities.silex_contract: World queries accept QueryFilter2D as a distinct typed filter with explicit defaults.

capabilities.capability: default typed joint configuration
capabilities.silex_contract: Eight typed settings construct joints and their handles retain the applicable runtime configuration.

capabilities.capability: default radial explosion configuration
capabilities.silex_contract: Explosion2DSettings provides typed defaults for filtered radial impulse gameplay.

capabilities.capability: default physics debug rendering configuration
capabilities.silex_contract: World2DDebugSettings will produce retained Canvas/Scene2D commands without native callbacks.

capabilities.capability: convex geometry construction and transforms
capabilities.silex_contract: Box2D, Polygon2D and Transform2D construct validated value geometry with input-order-independent convex hulls.

capabilities.capability: low-level convex proxy construction
capabilities.silex_contract: ShapePlacement2D accepts domain shapes and transforms while convex proxies remain private.
capabilities.rationale: The proxy is an algorithm input representation, not a gameplay concept that consumers need to own.

capabilities.capability: mass properties from collider geometry and density
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D derives composed mass, local center and inertia from living collider geometry and density.

capabilities.capability: shape and body world bounds
capabilities.silex_contract: Living colliders and bodies expose exact deterministic world bounds without proxy identities.

capabilities.capability: point containment against geometry and living colliders
capabilities.silex_contract: Geometry2D and Collider2D test finite points against value or living geometry.

capabilities.capability: closest points and distance between shapes
capabilities.silex_contract: Geometry2D.distance returns closest points, normal and non-negative separation over value placements.

capabilities.capability: ray casts against every convex shape
capabilities.silex_contract: Geometry2D.ray_cast handles every Shape2D placement and one-sided chains.

capabilities.capability: convex shape casts
capabilities.silex_contract: Geometry2D.shape_cast returns the earliest typed hit and supports controlled encroachment.

capabilities.capability: manifolds for all Box2D rigid-shape families
capabilities.silex_contract: Geometry2D exposes all geometric manifolds; every valid world pair will join one complete Soft Step response path.

capabilities.capability: sweep transform and time of impact
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D sweeps every fast dynamic convex collider against fixed and kinematic geometry; bullets extend the same resolved TOI path to dynamic targets.

capabilities.capability: collision-plane collection and clipped movement
capabilities.silex_contract: CharacterMover2D exposes separate plane collection, bounded resolution and vector clipping with value results instead of raw callbacks.

capabilities.capability: raw dynamic tree ownership and proxy operations
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D owns spatial acceleration privately and exposes gameplay queries over Collider2D handles.
capabilities.rationale: Proxy ids, user data, tree rebuilds and validation are storage and tuning mechanisms explicitly outside the public Silex contract.

capabilities.capability: world creation, validity and destruction
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D finalization follows the last reachable class reference and invalidates retained body, collider, chain and joint handles. World aliases and active calls preserve the world; snapshots preserve their values independently.
capabilities.rationale: Last-reference finalization replaces explicit C world destruction. The pinned oracle checks 44 observations, retaining 11 intentional differences: raw Box2D ids can become valid again after world-slot reuse; Silex handles preserve their old store identity and remain invalid. Application shutdown removes ECS-bound bodies; releasing the world invalidates every remaining handle. Cycles and reentrant callback release are qualified in Debug and Release.

capabilities.capability: deterministic world stepping
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D.step runs the native Soft Step graph with four default substeps or an explicit positive count. A zero-duration step preserves the last contact state and pending forces; refresh_contacts explicitly updates contacts while paused.

capabilities.capability: physics world debug rendering
capabilities.silex_contract: A reusable value snapshot will render through GFX.Canvas and GFX.Scene2D without native callbacks.

capabilities.capability: post-step movement, contact, hit and sensor streams
capabilities.silex_contract: Reusable post-step buffers avoid worker callbacks and retain deterministic collider snapshots for contact, hit and sensor streams.

capabilities.capability: overlap, ray and shape queries against living colliders
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D writes stable Collider2D results into caller-owned buffers and provides closest, any and all intentions.

capabilities.capability: capsule mover cast and collision planes
capabilities.silex_contract: CharacterMover2D collects, solves and reports a safe displaced capsule path without mutating the world.

capabilities.capability: sleep, warm start, restitution and speed tuning
capabilities.silex_contract: Typed, validated World2D settings expose sleep, continuous collision, restitution, contact tuning, speed limits and warm start with explicit wake policies.

capabilities.capability: read and change world gravity
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D accepts finite gravity at creation and exposes runtime reading and mutation with deterministic dynamic-body wakeup.

capabilities.capability: custom pair filtering, material combination and pre-solve
capabilities.silex_contract: Typed main-thread policies return immutable collider snapshots and explicit contact decisions without exposing callback context pointers.

capabilities.capability: radial world impulse
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D.explode aggregates collider contributions into deterministic typed body results.

capabilities.capability: awake counts, profiling and logical counters
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D exposes awake bodies, opt-in timings and live logical counters without internal array capacities.

capabilities.capability: untyped world user pointer
capabilities.silex_contract: World ownership stays in typed Silex values and resources.
capabilities.rationale: Untyped C pointers are explicitly outside the public contract.

capabilities.capability: static-tree rebuild, speculative test mode and memory dump
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D selects and maintains its acceleration and solver structures privately.
capabilities.rationale: These are diagnostic or implementation-tuning controls rather than stable gameplay intentions.

capabilities.capability: body creation, validity, ownership and destruction
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D owns stable invalidable RigidBody2D handles.

capabilities.capability: body transform, velocity, type, wake and bullet state
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D exposes direct motion and state mutations with explicit locking and wake semantics.

capabilities.capability: forces, torques, impulses, mass and inertia
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D exposes physical actions and composed or overridden mass without manual velocity integration.

capabilities.capability: local/world point, vector and point-velocity conversion
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D provides typed coordinate and point-velocity conversions.

capabilities.capability: damping, gravity, sleep, fixed rotation, activation and kinematic target
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D exposes validated runtime damping, gravity, sleep, fixed rotation, activation and kinematic target control outside step.

capabilities.capability: enumerate a body's living colliders
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D counts and writes stable Collider2D handles without exposing dense slots.

capabilities.capability: write current body contact data
capabilities.silex_contract: Bodies and colliders write completed manifold, impulse and resolved-material snapshots into caller-owned buffers.

capabilities.capability: enumerate a body's joints
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D writes a stable tagged Joint2D view for the whole world or one body while preserving typed handles.

capabilities.capability: body-wide contact and hit event toggles
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D toggles contact or hit events on all existing colliders, preserving independent flags and later creation settings. Each solid collider pair retains its own contact subscription from potential-contact creation.

capabilities.capability: body debug label
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D.debug_label provides typed diagnostics without C string lifetime rules.

capabilities.capability: untyped body user pointer
capabilities.silex_contract: RigidBody2D carries an optional uint64 application key, with immutable event snapshots and generation-safe invalidation.

capabilities.capability: living collider creation, identity, ownership and destruction
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D owns stable invalidable Collider2D handles distinct from Shape2D geometry values.

capabilities.capability: inspect and replace collider geometry
capabilities.silex_contract: Collider2D reads and replaces validated Shape2D values while retaining its living identity.

capabilities.capability: collider density, material, filter and sensor state
capabilities.silex_contract: Collider2DSettings and PhysicsMaterial2D own every surface and mass property per collider.

capabilities.capability: living collider ray cast and closest point
capabilities.silex_contract: Collider2D exposes local ray cast and world closest-point intentions with typed results.

capabilities.capability: per-collider contact, hit, pre-solve and sensor streams
capabilities.silex_contract: Collider2D owns contact, hit, sensor and pre-solve opt-ins; completed events, contacts and sensor overlaps retain deterministic collider identities.

capabilities.capability: untyped collider user pointer
capabilities.silex_contract: Collider2D carries its own optional uint64 application key independently of its body and material; snapshots preserve both object keys.

capabilities.capability: chain collider lifetime, segments and materials
capabilities.silex_contract: Collider2D retains one-sided Chain2D geometry with common or per-segment typed materials.

capabilities.capability: typed joint creation, validity and destruction
capabilities.silex_contract: World2D owns eight typed invalidable joint handles.
capabilities.rationale: The accepted Silex usage applies collision policy on the next step: a live filter joint removes existing contacts, and destroying a blocking joint requests rediscovery without artificial body movement. The filter lifetime acts as its switch; mechanical joints retain their collision setting. Twenty-four stages match an explicit public-API Box2D mapping while preserving nine raw-reference lifecycle differences.

capabilities.capability: joint bodies, kind, world, anchors, axis, reaction and separation
capabilities.silex_contract: Typed handles expose connected bodies, local frames, collision policy, wake, separation and completed-step reactions without solver state.
capabilities.rationale: The accepted Silex usage applies collision policy on the next step: a live filter joint removes existing contacts, and destroying a blocking joint requests rediscovery without artificial body movement. The filter lifetime acts as its switch; mechanical joints retain their collision setting. Twenty-four stages match an explicit public-API Box2D mapping while preserving nine raw-reference lifecycle differences. The accepted filtering adaptation is retained. Current measurements and family-specific constraint separation match 512 differential rows before stepping, after mutation and after stepping. Raw anchor vectors remain available separately.

capabilities.capability: recover the owning world from body, collider, chain and joint handles
capabilities.silex_contract: Consumers can explicitly retain or pass World2D alongside every handle family for creation, queries and destruction. A bare handle does not recover its world.
capabilities.rationale: The accepted Silex facade keeps World2D in the application scene or passes it explicitly with a handle for global operations. This uniform adaptation covers all four GetWorld symbols; a bare handle intentionally does not recover its world. World-wide invalidation remains a separate lifecycle obligation.

capabilities.capability: generic solver constraint tuning
capabilities.silex_contract: Distance, prismatic, revolute, weld and wheel expose common constraint hertz and damping independently of their springs and motors. Defaults, mutation, limits and fallback paths are compared at 1/2/4/8 substeps with central/offset anchors and one/two moving bodies.
capabilities.rationale: The tuning is consumed by these five reference joint families. Motor, mouse and filter do not use it in their solver. The typed facade omits their ineffective generic setting; their independent behavior has separate coverage.

capabilities.capability: complete runtime configuration for all eight joint families
capabilities.silex_contract: Each typed joint exposes its relevant limits, motors, springs, offsets, targets, maxima and measurements for validated runtime mutation.
capabilities.rationale: Motor/mouse transient response now has a complete 1536-sample differential witness alongside the five common-tuning families. Current length, translation, speed, angle and family-specific separation are qualified by 512 differential rows in Debug/Release, independently of completed-step reactions. Wheel translation/speed are checked against public body kinematics because the pinned version has no dedicated getters.

capabilities.capability: untyped joint user pointer
capabilities.silex_contract: All eight typed joint families carry optional uint64 application keys through creation, mutation, enumeration and destruction.
